entries.title: Steering: an open stage says plainly when its analysis still has to run
entries.summary: An open review stage or Stage 4 with no analysis imported now shows a highlighted "Next step: run the analysis" box instead of a grey note. The Ledger records how Stage 3 closed.
changes: Highlighted "Next step" box when a stage's analysis has not run
Stage 4 panel says the final read has not run and documents show as not read until it is imported
Ledger: Stage 3 close note

entries.title: Steering: import an analysis run from the steering page
entries.summary: Steering members can now import an analysis run from the open stage's tab: choose the run.json, check it with a dry run that writes nothing, then press Apply. No more shell pastes on the production server.
changes: Import box on open review stages and Stage 4
Dry-run report: fixes, analyses, batches, findings, documents checked, anything skipped
Bundles refresh after an import

entries.title: Steering: Stage 4 is the Final read
entries.summary: The last stage now reads each document's finished text once more before sign-off. Clean documents go straight to sign-off; anything found is settled in bundles (two members per fix or choice), and changed documents are re-checked round after round until a check finds nothing. Each document is then signed off by two members on its exact text.
changes: Stage 4 tab: the rounds so far, every document's status (findings to settle, needs a re-check, not read, ready to sign, signed off), a link to its full text and to sign off
Findings from every round appear in bundles, labelled by round
Sign-off is available only once a document's latest check matches its current text and nothing is open

entries.title: Steering: choosing a decision's recommended course covers its fixes
entries.summary: When a steering decision comes with drafted fixes (DP4's bold labels), choosing the recommended course now approves those fixes too, and "What needs you" counts them with the recommended fixes you can approve in one click. Members who already chose get an "Approve these" button on the fixes.
changes: Recording the recommended choice on a decision also casts your approve vote on its attached fixes
Fixes under a decision you chose count in "Approve all recommended fixes"
A line above a decision's fixes says how they relate to your choice

entries.title: Steering: a "What needs you" panel on each stage
entries.summary: Each review stage's bundles now open with a panel that says how many fixes wait for your vote, how many decisions wait for your choice and how many flagged changes you could review. One button approves every fix the analysis recommends as written, across all bundles, and "Show only what needs me" (on by default) hides everything else.
changes: "What needs you" counts fixes waiting for your vote, decisions waiting for your choice, and optional reviews
"Approve all N recommended fixes" records your accept vote on every open fix recommended as written, across all bundles; a second member still has to agree
"Show only what needs me" (on by default) shows only findings with something waiting for you, including fixes attached to decisions; "Include optional reviews" adds the flagged accepted changes
The bundle links at the top show how many findings in each need you

entries.title: Steering: a Ledger tab shows every stage in one table
entries.summary: /steering has a new Ledger tab to the right of Final: one row per stage with the same measures (dates, analysis, items in, findings, fixes filed, steering decisions, outcome), plus notes for each stage. Dates and outcomes come live from Gov Hub; the analysis figures are recorded as each stage runs.
changes: New Ledger tab after Final (?stage=ledger)
Dates and outcomes are live; analysis figures live in src/data/steering-ledger.json

entries.title: Steering: every review stage is worked in bundles
entries.summary: Each review stage tab (Stage 2: Cross-DP, Stage 3: Style) now shows its analysis's findings as bundles, one box per kind of fix across the chapters. Until a stage's analysis is run, the tab says so. Settled bundles disappear unless "Show settled bundles" is ticked, and a bundle with nothing left for you folds to one line.
changes: A review stage whose analysis has not been run says so, with the chapters behind a toggle
Each bundle has its own box with its findings, fixes and "Approve all as written" where the analysis recommends it
Settled bundles are hidden unless "Show settled bundles" is ticked; a bundle with nothing left for you folds to one line (Show / Collapse)
A closed review stage (Stage 2) keeps its bundles, read-only, for anyone signed in

entries.title: Steering: a cross-DP finding is settled once its fixes are decided
entries.summary: On the Stage 2 issues view, a finding with fixes now counts as settled (and is hidden unless "Show settled findings" is on) once every fix is accepted, deferred or declined, even if the accepted changes it flagged were not reviewed one by one. Those changes are kept when the stage closes unless someone defers them.
changes: A finding with fixes is settled when all its fixes are decided
A finding without fixes is still settled once the changes it flagged are reviewed

entries.title: Steering: what you have answered folds away
entries.summary: In every stage, a fix, an accepted change, a batch or a decision you have already voted on now folds to one line showing your vote and where it stands, so what still needs you stays in view. Each folded line opens again with Show.
changes: Fixes and proposals you voted on (or that are carried out) fold to one line with your vote and their state
Accepted changes you reviewed, batches you approved and decisions you chose fold the same way
On the Stage 2 issues view, a finding folds once every fix, flagged change and decision under it has your answer
Show opens a folded card; Collapse folds it again

entries.title: Steering: members are recognised even after their sign-in refreshes
entries.summary: /steering could show a steering member the read-only view when the page was rendered with a sign-in that had expired. It now also trusts the membership Gov Hub reports with the stage data, so steering members see the Stage 2 issues view and the stage controls.
changes: /steering uses the steering flag from the overview data as well as the page's own check

entries.title: Steering: the Stage 2 tab is worked by issue
entries.summary: For steering members, the Stage 2: Cross-DP tab on /steering now shows the cross-DP findings to settle (the fix bundles and the decisions) instead of every chapter's carried items. A group of fixes that the analysis recommends as written can be approved in one click.
changes: The Stage 2 tab shows the cross-DP issues in place of the chapter lists; carried items by chapter are one click away
"Approve all as written" records your accept vote on every open fix in a group that the analysis recommends as written; a second member still has to agree
Findings with nothing left to vote on are hidden with the settled ones
Accepted changes the cross-DP check found no issue with need no vote: any not reviewed are kept when the stage closes

entries.title: Steering: vote and comment on the cross-DP decisions
entries.summary: On /steering/issues, each finding that needs a steering decision now lists its options, with the review's recommendation, and steering members choose one. Two members choosing the same course settle it. Every finding also takes comments from steering members.
changes: Each decision lists the review's options, plus Defer to 1.1 and Something else (with a note saying what)
Two steering members choosing the same course settle the decision; a member can change or withdraw their choice
Steering members can comment on any finding and remove their own comments
A settled decision records the choice only: any text change it calls for is filed and voted as a proposal

entries.title: Steering: Stage 2 opens alongside Stage 1 and is organised by issue
entries.summary: Steering can now open Stage 2 while Stage 1 still has proposals to settle. Everything Stage 1 has accepted flows into Stage 2 as it is accepted. Stage 2 has a new page, organised by issue: each cross-DP finding sits in one of four groups with the fixes that settle it, so a finding and its fixes are read and voted on together.
changes: "Open Stage 2 now" on /steering, for steering members. It is a deliberate step, not automatic
With both stages open, new community proposals still land in Stage 1 and the fixes the cross-DP review files land in Stage 2. Stages close in order: Stage 1 first
New page /steering/issues: findings grouped as Broken text, Pointers and titles, Meaning, and Steering decisions, each with the fixes that settle it and any accepted change it flags
Every fix card on the issues page has "Ask Deepi about this proposal" for steering members
Settled findings are hidden by default, with a switch to show them
The Stage 1 record keeps only Stage 1's items and the analysis they were decided on

entries.title: Steering: batches name what is left to vote on
entries.summary: A partly finished batch now names the items that still need your vote, each linking to its card. The cards already carried out are collapsed under one line, so a done card no longer sits above the Approve button looking like the item being voted on.
changes: Partly finished batches list the items that still need your vote, with links to their cards.
Cards already carried out are collapsed under one line below the open ones.

entries.title: Steering: four stages, with accepted changes carried forward
entries.summary: Passes are now a fixed plan of four stages: Stage 1 proposal review, Stage 2 cross-DP, Stage 3 style, and Final. Whatever a stage accepts opens in the next stage to be reviewed again against that stage's analysis. Final is a sign-off by two steering members on each document's finished text. A stage closes only when nothing is open, and each closed stage keeps a public, read-only record.
changes: Stage tabs on /steering: Stage 1: Proposal review, Stage 2: Cross-DP, Stage 3: Style, Final. Stages still to come are listed but can't be opened yet (?stage=stage-1)
Accepted items move on: when a stage closes, what it accepted appears in the next stage under "Carried into", with the earlier decision, votes and analysis attached

Each carried item gets three choices: Keep, Keep with a follow-up edit, or Defer to 1.1. The last two need a note. Two members settle each item, and nothing is reverted: a follow-up edit or an undo is filed as a new proposal
"Keep all with no issue found" keeps, in one click, every carried item that this stage's analysis checked and found no problem with. Flagged and unchecked items are reviewed one by one
A stage closes only when nothing is open. Remaining proposals can be deferred to 1.1 as part of closing, keeping their votes. Carried items nobody reviewed are kept
Final: two steering members sign off each document's finished text. A sign-off is tied to the exact text, so any later change voids it
Ask Deepi can now answer questions about carried items too

entries.title: Steering: four stages, with accepted changes carried forward
entries.summary: Passes are now a fixed plan of four stages: Stage 1 proposal review, Stage 2 cross-DP, Stage 3 style, and Final. Whatever a stage accepts opens in the next stage to be reviewed again against that stage's analysis. Final is a sign-off by two steering members on each document's finished text. A stage closes only when nothing is open, and each closed stage keeps a public, read-only record.
changes: Stage tabs on /steering: Stage 1: Proposal review, Stage 2: Cross-DP, Stage 3: Style, Final. Stages still to come are listed but can't be opened yet (?stage=stage-1)
Accepted items move on: when a stage closes, what it accepted appears in the next stage under "Carried into", with the earlier decision, votes and analysis attached

Each carried item gets three choices: Keep, Keep with a follow-up edit, or Defer to 1.1. The last two need a note. Two members settle each item, and nothing is reverted: a follow-up edit or an undo is filed as a new proposal

Final: two steering members sign off each document's finished text. A sign-off is tied to the exact text, so any later change voids it
Ask Deepi can now answer questions about carried items too

entries.title: Steering: passes (Pass 1, Pass 2, Final), each with a public record once closed
entries.summary: The steering page now has a tab for each pass. Closing a pass saves its full record (every proposal with its analysis, votes and outcome), makes that record public and read-only, carries open items into the next pass and opens it. Anyone signed in can follow the open pass's progress; only steering members open its documents and see the steering notes.
changes: Pass tabs on /steering; the open pass shows live progress, a closed pass shows its saved record (?pass=pass-1)
Each document row and the totals show Open, Accepted, Deferred and Declined counts in colored circles
Close Pass (steering members): name the next pass, say what it covers, and leave a closing note that is public with the record
Items still open when a pass closes are carried into the next pass with their votes and marked "Carried from"
A closed pass's documents (/steering/<ml>?pass=<key>) are readable by anyone, read-only, without voting or Ask Deepi
Anyone signed in sees the steering overview; steering notes and the audit export stay steering-only

entries.title: Steering: Open, Accepted, Deferred and Declined tabs
entries.summary: Each steering document page now splits its proposals into Open, Accepted, Deferred and Declined tabs, each with its count in a colored circle, so what still needs a decision is easy to see.
changes: Open lists the batches and items still to decide; a batch shows only its open items
Accepted (accept and accept revised), Deferred and Declined list what was carried out
An outcome that failed to apply stays under Open
The tab is kept in ?tab= so a reload or a shared link opens the same one
Wording now says two steering members must agree, since steering has five members

entries.title: Workgroup chat: clickable links, opens at the newest message
entries.summary: Links in workgroup chat messages are now clickable, and the chat opens at the newest message and stays there when you post or new messages arrive.
changes: http(s) and www. links in chat messages (and steering notes) open in a new tab; trailing punctuation is left out of the link
The message list opens scrolled to the newest message
Posting a message scrolls to it; new messages keep the list at the bottom while you are reading there, but not when you have scrolled up
Permalinks (?m=) and the "New messages" line still decide where the chat opens when they apply

entries.title: Ask Deepi on steering can look across the whole book
entries.summary: When a steering member asks Deepi about a proposal or batch, Deepi can now search every document in the book and look up proposals on other documents, so it can say whether another chapter already covers, repeats or contradicts a change.
changes: Lookups Deepi can make while answering: search the current text of all 28 documents, read a range of blocks, list the open proposals on any document, and open one proposal with its analysis and votes
Read-only, using the asking member's own Gov Hub access; the book text is cached for five minutes
Answers cite other documents by ML number and block, e.g. ML-Draft-013 [40]
Up to six rounds of lookups per question; the knowledge graph (Hermes) is not used yet

entries.title: Workgroup chat: attach files, times in your timezone
entries.summary: Workgroup members can attach documents and images to a chat message, and message times now show in the reader's own timezone instead of UTC.
changes: Chat composer: "Attach file" button; PDF, Word (.docx), PNG or JPEG, up to 3 files, 10 MB each (15 MB total); a message can be just files
Attachments on member messages show as download links, like emailed reviews; members only
Gov Hub timestamps without a zone are read as UTC by the shared date formatter, so chat times (and other dates it formats) appear in local time
Needs the matching Gov Hub release (multipart uploads on POST /api/workgroups/<id>/messages/)

entries.title: Steering notes chat
entries.summary: A private chat on the steering pages where the three steering committee members can leave each other notes. Only the committee can read it; notes are not votes.
changes: /steering and /steering/<ml>: "Steering notes" chat at the bottom, one shared thread
Notes written from a document page are tagged with that document and link back to it; a document page can show only its own notes
Authors can remove their own notes (soft delete); refreshes every 30 seconds
New API /api/steering/notes (steering members only, checked with Gov Hub); notes stored in dp_steering_note

entries.title: Ask Deepi on the steering pages
entries.summary: Steering committee members can ask Deepi (Claude Opus 5.5) about a whole batch or a single proposal before voting. Deepi reads the analysis, the votes so far, the document text and the style guide. Each member's questions are private, with a daily limit.
changes: /steering/<ml>: "Ask Deepi about this batch" under each batch summary
/steering/<ml>: "Ask Deepi about this proposal" on each item card, under the analysis
New API /api/steering/<ml>/ask (steering members only; Gov Hub checks)

Review tab after the freeze: recommendation and vote state per item; Approve and Decline record steering votes

changes: WorkgroupReviewPanel reloads the review queue when the signed-in user changes

entries.title: Readiness board: proposals by DP, with totals

entries.title: Workgroup chat: see which messages you haven't read

entries.title: Workgroup pages: an MTP tab for each chapter's Massive Transformational Purpose

entries.title: Style guide for the Desirable Properties book
entries.summary: A new page, /style-guide, sets how the book is written so 23 chapters read as one: who we write for, voice, requirement language (MUST/SHOULD/MAY), chapter structure, headings, terms, formatting, cross-references, sources, how to write a patch or insert, and guidance for co-editors. Most rules record what the chapters already do; the rest settle where they disagree. The same rules are available as text for the upcoming AI check of patches and inserts.
changes: New /style-guide page: 11 sections, 49 rules, with do/don't examples drawn from the book
Rules derived from a count across all 23 live chapters (e.g. 115 capital MUST/SHOULD inside '(Non-Normative)' sections; Meta-Layer spelled two ways)
styleGuideAsText() exports the guide for AI review prompts
Linked from the About menu, /process, and the Review tab's decision note
entries.verify: Open /style-guide: eleven sections from 'Who we write for' to 'For co-editors'; About menu lists Style guide.
entries.intent: Consistent tone and style across chapters, agreed at the 12 Oct 2026 session; the basis for the AI pre-check of manual patches and inserts.

entries.title: Workgroup cards show co-editor staffing, not a 3-member target
entries.summary: Workgroup cards on /workgroups now read, for example, '2 members · co-editors 0 of 2' or '4 members · fully staffed', instead of 'needs 1 more for a working group'. The 3-member target is gone from the workgroups intro, Start Here and the workgroup Getting Started tab; the Co-editors section above the tabs covers staffing.
changes: DP cards: member count plus co-editor seats from the readiness data; amber until two co-editors, green when fully staffed
DP Discovery card: member count only (it has no co-editors)
Workgroups intro and Start Here: 'at least 3 people' replaced with the two-co-editor rule
Getting Started tab: member-target box removed
entries.verify: Open /workgroups: each DP card shows 'n members · co-editors x of 2' or 'fully staffed'; no card mentions 'more for a working group'.
entries.intent: Two co-editors, not a member count, is what makes a DP fully staffed.

entries.title: Becoming a co-editor is easy to find; '3 members' check removed
entries.summary: The Co-editors card now sits above the workgroup tabs and says plainly how many co-editors the DP needs, with a 'Become a co-editor' button, what the role involves, and why you can't take a seat when you can't. Workgroup cards on /workgroups link straight to it. The 'Workgroup has at least 3 members' readiness item is gone; two co-editors is what makes a DP fully staffed.
changes: Co-editors card moved from the bottom of the header to its own section above the tabs
'Claim a seat' renamed 'Become a co-editor', with what the role involves and a character countdown
Shows why a seat can't be taken (already a co-editor, seats taken, account under 7 days, per-person limit)
Co-editors see a link to the Review tab; 'Nominate them' for members
Header 'Nominate' is now 'Nominate coordinator'; /workgroups cards get 'Become a co-editor'
Readiness: 'at least 3 members' removed from the card, board and process page
entries.verify: Signed in, open a DP workgroup page: the Co-editors section is above the tabs with 'Become a co-editor'. Needs Gov Hub #16 (bearer-token seat routes).
entries.intent: Members must be able to see and take an open co-editor seat without hunting for it.

entries.title: Invite with Email: events and perspectives load again
entries.summary: On production the Invite with Email tab showed 'The string did not match the expected pattern' instead of the events and perspectives you can include. A one-off rename of the 'Fork in the Web' perspective ran on every request and, when both the old and new entries existed, broke the unique-name rule each time. The rename now runs only when it is safe, the list loads even if one part fails, and a failure shows a plain message saying the invitation can still be sent.
changes: Perspective rename runs on one row and only when the new name is free; first-run seed ignores duplicates
Rename and seed run once per server process instead of on every request
/api/invite-content returns whatever loaded and logs what failed, instead of a bare 500
Invite tab shows a readable message when the list cannot load, instead of Safari's JSON parse error
entries.verify: curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://desirableproperties.org/api/invite-content returns 200, and the Invite with Email tab lists events and perspectives.
entries.intent: Inviting people to workgroups must not be blocked or confused by optional content failing to load.

entries.title: Co-editors: coordinator seat, claim or nominate; a no needs a reason
entries.summary: Each workgroup page now has a Co-editors card showing the DP's two seats. The coordinator holds one seat automatically; the other is claimed, or a member nominates someone who becomes co-editor the moment they accept. On the Review tab, Decline stays disabled until the co-editor writes a note the author can read. Two co-editors now mean a DP is fully staffed; the 3-member check is shown for context only.
changes: New Co-editors card on each workgroup page: seats, Claim a seat, Nominate a member, Revoke
Co-editor removed from the generic Nominate dropdown (coordinator nominations only)
Review tab: Approve / Decline with a decision note; Decline is disabled until the note has text, and the note is sent to Gov Hub
Readiness board: 'fully staffed' = both co-editor seats; member count no longer counts toward Ready
Process, workgroups, FAQ and role copy updated for the new seat rules and the agreed 7-day decision rule
entries.verify: On a DP workgroup page the Co-editors card shows 'n of 2'. On the Review tab, Decline is greyed out until text is typed in Decision note. Requires the matching Gov Hub release (feature/co-editor-nominations).
entries.intent: Implements the co-editor decisions from the 12 Oct 2026 DP session: coordinators are co-editors, seats are claimed or nominated (opt-in), and every rejection carries a rationale.

entries.title: Sign-in uses each site's own Web3Auth ID
entries.summary: The site no longer falls back to production's Web3Auth client ID. Production and staging each name their own ID, and if the ID is missing, sign-in shows a clear error instead of quietly using production's.
changes: Removed the hardcoded production client ID from the Web3Auth config and token check
Production and staging pm2 configs each set their own WEB3AUTH_CLIENT_ID_DEVNET
A missing ID now returns a clear error on sign-in; other pages still load
entries.verify: Open sign-in on staging.desirableproperties.org: the Web3Auth config endpoint returns the staging ID (BL4DIH…), and production returns BKvRj4….
entries.intent: Staging and production each use their own Web3Auth project; a missing ID must fail loudly, never fall back to production's.

entries.title: Email key no longer kept in the code
entries.summary: The web app's setup and email-test scripts now read the Resend email key from the server environment instead of having it written into the code. The two keys that were in the code had already been switched off in Resend. No visible change on the site.
changes: create-env.sh writes RESEND_API_KEY from the environment and warns if it is missing
test-resend.js reads RESEND_API_KEY from the environment and stops if it is missing
The old keys stay in git history but no longer work
entries.intent: No secrets in the source of a public repo.

entries.title: Merging to main now deploys the site
entries.summary: The site and the book are deployed by production itself when a change is merged, instead of by GitHub logging into the old server. The old deploy jobs pointed at a server that is being retired, so they were removed. No visible change on the site.
changes: Removed the deploy-challenge-site and deploy-webapp workflows, which deployed to the retired server
The rail-sync workflow still syncs and commits; production publishes the book when that commit lands
Runtime files written on the server (loop state and logs, script cache) are ignored by git
entries.verify: After a merge to main, /var/log/pull-deploy/desirable-properties.log on production shows DEPLOY and OK for the new commit
entries.intent: Production deploys itself from main; GitHub holds no credential that reaches the server.

entries.title: Gov Hub links open the current draft, on interfacehub.net
entries.summary: Workgroup activity links now open the latest approved revision of each DP draft on Gov Hub instead of the original Revision 00. Every remaining hub.themetalayer.org link now points to interfacehub.net.
changes: Workgroup activity feed links drafts by ML number, so Gov Hub serves the current revision
hub.themetalayer.org and dev.hub.themetalayer.org replaced with interfacehub.net and dev.interfacehub.net across the site, book viewer, inscription data, welcome content, scripts and docs
Framing chapter link uses ML-Draft-026 instead of a pinned row id, so it follows new revisions
entries.intent: People who click through to patch a DP should land on the text the book shows, not an outdated revision.
entries.verify: Open a DP workgroup page and follow a draft link in its activity feed: it should open the current revision on interfacehub.net.

entries.title: Turn a Deepi conversation into a Canopi comment
entries.summary: Under Deepi's latest reply you can now draft a Canopi comment from that turn or from the whole thread. Deepi offers three versions (builder, steward, skeptic); you edit one, choose page comment, reply or quote, and post it under your own name, marked AI-assisted.
changes: Comment from this turn / from the whole thread buttons on Deepi's latest reply
Three perspective drafts, editable, with page / reply / quote targets
Posted as the signed-in person via their Canopi session, with aiAssist provenance
entries.intent: Help people bring what they worked out with Deepi into the community conversation, in their own words.

entries.title: Canopi chapter feeds cached and rate-capped
entries.summary: Activity and search read every chapter's Canopi feed on each call. Those reads are now cached for 60 seconds and at most 4 run at once, so the site no longer floods Canopi (about 2,600 requests in 4 minutes on 2026-09-25) and Canopi's sidebar stays fast.
changes: 60 s cache per chapter feed, shared by concurrent callers; failed reads are not cached
At most 4 Canopi feed requests in flight per server process
Test: npm run test:canopi-feed-cache
entries.intent: Stop DP from slowing Canopi for everyone (canopi#32).

entries.title: Estate changelog adopted
entries.summary: Desirable Properties now keeps a volunteer-readable change log that agents and meta-console can parse.
changes: Added changelog.json in estate-changelog/v1 form
CI fails PRs that change watched paths without a changelog entry
entries.intent: Start a human and machine changelog for challenge-site deploys
